# A cover-hinge inequality retaining the supporting-fiber force

Use the notation and proved duality of
`candidate b4c3b9c6a52059d2`.
Fix a positive integer fiber K=C_j and 0<t<=T_max(j), and let
M=M_t(j) subset K be its compact base-balanced source moment body.

Consider finitely many closed ambient caps

 H_i={u_i.x+a_i.(z-j)-b_i>=0},  i=1,...,N,

and define their nonnegative hinge costs

 Psi_i=integral [u_i.x+a_i.(z-j)-b_i]_+ dmu.         (1)

For any nonnegative weights lambda_i, the support dual gives

 sum_i lambda_i Psi_i
    >=t[sum_i lambda_i h_M(u_i)-sum_i lambda_i b_i]. (2)

In particular a positive circuit with sum lambda_i u_i=0 and
sum lambda_i b_i<=0 has a nonnegative right side. The following
version also handles cover certificates with a nonzero resultant
normal, including those supported by the boundary of K.

## 1. Exact full-fiber minimax certificate

Define the coverage margin

 phi=min_(x in K) max_i(u_i.x-b_i).                  (3)

The caps cover the entire fiber {j}xK if and only if phi>=0. Compactness
gives the minimum, and continuity makes this statement include closed
boundary contacts.

There are weights lambda_i>=0 summing to one such that, with
ubar=sum_i lambda_i u_i,

 phi=-h_K(-ubar)-sum_i lambda_i b_i.                (4)

Here is a finite-dimensional proof. The affine map
x -> (u_i.x-b_i)_i sends K to a compact convex set A in R^N. By the
definition of phi, A is disjoint from the open lower orthant
O={v:v_i<phi for every i}. Separate the compact convex set A from O.
The separating normal lambda has nonnegative coordinates because O
is unbounded in every negative coordinate direction. It is nonzero,
so normalize its sum to one. The supremum of lambda.v on O is phi.
Thus min_(v in A) lambda.v>=phi. Conversely the point of A which
minimizes max_i v_i has every coordinate at most phi, so its lambda
average is at most phi. Equality follows, giving (4) after minimizing
ubar.x over K. No interior covering margin or general position is
needed for this argument.

## 2. The supporting force remains in the hinge lower bound

Choose the weights furnished by (4). Substitution into (2) proves

 sum_i lambda_i Psi_i
   >=t[phi+h_K(-ubar)+sum_i lambda_i h_M(u_i)]       (5)
   >=t[phi+h_K(-ubar)-h_M(-ubar)].                  (6)

For the second inequality, sublinearity gives
sum lambda_i h_M(u_i)>=h_M(ubar), and the support-width inequality
h_M(ubar)+h_M(-ubar)>=0 completes the claim. Since M subset K, the
support difference in (6) is nonnegative.

The uncontracted term in (5) often carries more information than (6).
For example, suppose M contains a Euclidean ball of radius r>=0
centered at p, and every continuous normal has |u_i|=1. Then

 sum lambda_i h_M(u_i)>=ubar.p+r,
 h_K(-ubar)>=-ubar.p,

and therefore

 sum_i lambda_i Psi_i>=t(phi+r).                  (7)

Thus a full-fiber cover gives a positive lower bound tr whenever this
common moment body has positive inradius. This conclusion keeps the
supporting-fiber normal ubar rather than setting it to zero.

## 3. Scope

All the hinge costs in (1) are measured against the same original
mixed measure; every cap keeps its own integer coefficient a_i.
Equation (2) applies the exact support dual separately to each actual
cap, but it does not minimize an integer tilt independently at every
threshold inside its hinge integral. The common body M provides the
cross-direction compatibility used in (5).

This lower bound does not by itself contradict a prescribed upper
bound on the cap VOLUMES. Hinge costs also contain the distances of
retained points from the cap boundaries. No inequality converting
an arbitrary common cap-volume budget into a conflicting hinge
upper bound is asserted here. The result is the exact cover-hinge
bridge, including all supporting-fiber forces.
